native_result.query: In what context does the gardening pathway for introducing non-native plants show different prevalence styles across habitat types?
native_result.HypoA: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats.
native_result.HypoB: The gardening pathway for introducing non-native plants shows habitat-context-dependent prevalence styles: it is the dominant-but-sparse pathway in semi-natural habitats (broad-leaved/coniferous forests, wetlands, coastal; 54-100% of non-native occurrences, present in nearly every invaded plot, 1.3-1.4 gardening species per invaded plot) where invasions are rare but gardening-dominated; it becomes abundant-but-subordinate to the Unintentional pathway in anthropized habitats (urban 29.8%, croplands 18.5% share; mean 0.83/0.39 gardening vs 1.93/1.63 unintentional species per invaded plot); and its species are tall woody perennials with the narrowest invaded niches (0.449 vs 0.749), while temporally the pathway surged from 16.8% to 75.2% of new introductions across the four periods - a modern, deliberate, structural-invader prevalence style that contrasts with the widespread generalist style of unintentional introductions.
native_result.WorkflowB: Executed analysis.py on the 4 staged assets. (A) Temporal prevalence: 4x3 period x pathway chi-square + shares (temporal_trends). (B) Compositional prevalence: 10x3 habitat x pathway species-occurrence table (invaded_niche n.gard/n.unint/n.agfo summed per habitat, n.total internally verified), chi2_contingency + 200,000-iteration unconditional Monte-Carlo p (sparse-cell robust), Cramer's V, adjusted standardized residuals, per-habitat enrichment vs 0.351 overall share and 1-df chi-square, plus 9x3 sensitivity dropping Rock outcrops. (C) Per-plot intensity/occupancy: mean n.gard and n.unint among invaded plots and gardening occupancy per habitat. (D) Species-level: 77 species after de-duplicating the 4 duplicated=TRUE records; pathway means, Kruskal-Wallis and pairwise Mann-Whitney (Bonferroni x2) on invaded.niche.breadth, habitat.range, n.invaded.plots, AOO, mrt, height, native.niche.breadth; growth-form/dispersal crosstabs. (E) Context model (supporting, descriptive): penalized (ridge) logistic of per-plot gardening presence ~ habitat (reference Urban) + elevation + urban.2009.1000m + cropland.2009.1000m + progressive.1993.2009.50m + log distance-to-road + annual temperature, on all 632 plots and on the 191 invaded plots; penalization used because sparse/zero cells cause quasi-separation in unpenalized ML; coefficients read as directions only. (F) Phylogeny: Newick parsed to verify 77/77 (81/81) species tip coverage; optional Mantel permutation test (9,999 perms) of phylogenetic distance vs |invaded niche breadth difference| among 39 gardening species (r=0.014, p=0.353). Formal PGLS is NOT performed (no R/phylolm in runtime) - trait contrasts are descriptive with the Mantel check as a caveat.
